title: Erase one array position and preserve order
prompt: Erase index from a vector<int>, shift later values left, and return true. If index is outside the live range, return false without changing the vector. Do not erase every occurrence of that value.

tests.label: First
tests.hint: The first removal shifts all later items.

tests.label: Last
tests.hint: No shifting is needed at the last index.

tests.label: Empty
tests.hint: Index zero is invalid for an empty vector.

hints: The loop begins one item after the removed position.
Only shorten the vector after shifting.
explanation: The invariant is that the kept prefix stays in its old order and each suffix item moves left once. vector::erase is the simpler real-world alternative. Swapping with the last item is faster but changes order. The starter removes 9 rather than 8 in the sample and outputs 7 8. State whether order matters before choosing a faster removal.
chapterTitle: Understanding Arrays and Contiguous Dynamic Storage
